questions.prompt: Which Figma tool gives a sparse XML outline with layer IDs, names, types, position and sizes?

options.explanation: Right. Figma describes it as a sparse XML representation of your selection.
This returns a picture of the selection, not an outline.
This returns the variables and styles used in a selection.

questions.prompt: Why can a screenshot alone give code that does not use your tokens?

options.text: Screenshots are always too blurry for a model to see any colour
options.explanation: The colour is visible. The name behind it is not.

options.text: The model does not get file names or metadata from an image
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's vision page says this. A screenshot holds only pixels. The token name lives in the Figma file, not in the picture.

options.text: Design servers block screenshots, so the model reads nothing
options.explanation: Figma has a screenshot tool and recommends keeping it on.

questions.prompt: What does Canva's get-design-content tool return?

options.text: Every element with an ID, ready for editing
options.explanation: Canva says editable element IDs come from start-editing-transaction, not this tool.

options.text: A full-page PNG export at print quality
options.explanation: Exports are a different tool. This one reads text.

options.text: The design's text as one field, plus metadata
options.explanation: Right. Canva says it is for reading content, not for targeting edits.
